notes.which: Only streaks of {{min}} matches or more are shown ({{fallback}} if very few appear) that would happen by chance at most 1 in {{chance}} times, one per team and market (the one with the most demanding line) and at most {{perEntity}} per team and day. Matches from the same competition count, from this season and the previous one. Referee streaks only once the referee has been appointed.
notes.cards: Cards and booking points come from our data: cards = yellows + reds; points = yellow 10, red 25 (approximate). A statistic a league doesn't have isn't shown, and a match without the data doesn't break the streak.

rarity.title: What is rarity?
rarity.what: Rarity measures how hard it would be to see a streak like that <bold>by pure chance</bold>, if the team were just any side in the league. It's calculated from the league's usual rate for that event, multiplied by itself as many times as there are matches in the streak. It's the ‘By chance’ figure on each row: ‘1 in 1,500’ means that, by pure luck, only 1 team in 1,500 would have a streak like that.
rarity.example1: Winning 8 in a row when 40% of matches in the league are won: 0.40<sup>8</sup> ≈ 1 in 1,500. Very rare.
rarity.example2: 9 in a row of something that happens 90% of the time: 0.90<sup>9</sup> ≈ 1 in 3. That's normal, so it doesn't appear in the table.
rarity.example3: 6 in a row of something that happens half the time: 0.50<sup>6</sup> ≈ 1 in 64. It's shorter than the previous one but much rarer: that's why it comes first.
rarity.order: That's why ‘Rarest first’ doesn't sort by length: that way, long streaks of things that almost always happen don't rise to the top.
rarity.notSay: <bold>What it doesn't say:</bold> it isn't the probability of the streak continuing. It assumes the team is an average one and that each match is independent, which isn't always the case: a team that shoots a lot almost always does, and its streak can come out extremely rare without being any surprise. If you want to know whether streaks continue, see ‘Do streaks continue?’ at the bottom of the page. <anchor>More in the glossary →</anchor>

study.title: Do streaks continue?
study.method: Using matches from {{seasons}} ({{leagues}}): before each match, the streaks this table would have shown ({{min}} matches or more, calculated using earlier matches only) and whether they continued in that match, compared with the league's usual rate up to then for that same event. In brackets, the difference with its 95% interval (resampling matches, {{samples}} samples, fixed seed). No data: fewer than {{minEvents}} streaks.
study.empty: Not enough matches to measure it.
study.verdictNone: No clear difference: with this data, streaks continued at roughly the league's usual rate.
study.verdictAbove: In {{above}} of {{cells}} cells the streak clearly continued more often than the league's usual rate; in the rest there's no clear difference. Continuing more often than the league average isn't momentum: above all, it says that team isn't an average one in that market.
study.verdictAboveBelow: In {{above}} of {{cells}} cells the streak clearly continued more often than the league's usual rate and in {{below}}, less often; in the rest there's no clear difference. Continuing more often than the league average isn't momentum: above all, it says that team isn't an average one in that market.
